adjudications.reason: Rank 1 (MathArrays.mostFrequent, gold second, facade third) rests on chain item 2's role premise: mostFrequent is 'the most direct method responsible for forming the returned mode array'. That premise cites no documentation of mostFrequent (its javadoc, 'most frequently occurring value(s) ... in ascending order', is silent on NaN and literally satisfied by [NaN]), no oddity in its body (the reverse-index copy was requested at calls 4 and 12 but is never described beyond 'converts Frequency.getMode() directly to a double array'), and no name match (the ranking reason is functional, although the first grep for 'double[] mode' at call 2 surfaced MathArrays:1538 and call 4 read mostFrequent alongside the facade before any hop was traced). Item 3 states that tabulate 'adds every double value to Frequency without checking Double.isNaN' and that 'a missing NaN filter before frequency counting' causes the result: the agent located the omission at the gold (requested at calls 8 and 12; 'new Frequency' pinned to FastMath:1138 at call 14; frozen full_gold_read=true) and still ranked another hop first. None of CONVENTION_PRIOR, LOCAL_ODDNESS_BIAS or LEXICAL_SHORTCUT is supported by the stated reason, so ATTRIBUTION_FAILURE is primary. CONVENTION_PRIOR is secondary because item 1 frames the culprit as 'the mode implementation' violating StatUtils.mode's documented contract and item 2 nominates mostFrequent as that implementation: contract ownership transferred to the mode-forming hop although nothing there documents a NaN rule. The process lens's EVIDENCE_INTEGRATION_FAILURE secondary is rejected: the decisive evidence (unguarded loop; NaN counted as a mode key in FrequencyTest.testModeDoubleNan at call 11; four NaNs versus three 0s and 2s at call 10) was used in item 3, so the failure is in the ranking step, not in integration. Not defensible: mostFrequent carries no NaN obligation, and a post-count filter there cannot yield [0, 2] once NaN (4) out-counts 0 and 2 (3 each); the only fix sites are tabulate's loop or a pre-delegation filter at the documented facade.

Both labellers agree ENTRY_POINT_BIAS and CONVENTION_PRIOR apply and that the chain located the divergence at the gold (item 3: 'FastMath.tabulate unconditionally adds every Double value, including NaN, to a Frequency' and 'NaNs are counted before mode selection'; tabulate requested in full at call 10 of 15, nl 1100-1165, frozen gold_exposed=true). The split is only primary order. The agent's sole rank-1 justification is item 1: 'The public mode API is not honoring its documented NaN-ignore behavior', candidate_methods [StatUtils::mode], references StatUtils.java 808-823 (the javadoc NaN clause plus the delegating body). The load-bearing predicate is the documented behaviour, not that the test calls it or that it is the repair site, so under the adjudication rule CONVENTION_PRIOR is primary and ENTRY_POINT_BIAS secondary ('public mode API'; first code read was the entry point at call 4; calls 11-14 returned to StatUtils imports and callers rather than to tabulate's callers). Partly defensible: StatUtils.mode is the only method on the path whose javadoc promises NaN exclusion and it returns NaN on the trigger, but its body is a null check plus a one-line delegation (line 822; the begin/length overload at 859 shares the path), so the omitted guard is tabulate's and no statement in mode is wrong.

The extended view overturns the premise of the process label. Call 8 (nl -ba FastMath.java | grep -n 'tabulate' -A120 -B20) displayed the whole method, lines 1130-1144, including 1140 'final double value = values[i];' and 1141 'freq.addValue(Double.valueOf(value));', thirteen calls before the submission at call 21. The safe view's cut at the signature is a view artefact; frozen gold_exposed=false and full_gold_read=false are wrong for this run. DISCOVERY_WITHOUT_INSPECTION is therefore not warranted. EVIDENCE_INTEGRATION_FAILURE is warranted: having displayed the unguarded loop, the agent spent calls 9-20 on jshell probes of StatUtils.mode only (call 10), Frequency excerpts that never reach getMode (calls 11-13), StatUtils imports (calls 15-16) and MathArrays greps, and its chain never states that tabulate omits the isNaN check; item 2 hedges between 'the public mode method's NaN filtering' and 'the helper that tabulates', so the divergence was not located at the gold. The rank-1 choice itself is justified by repair location at the public method ('Any fix is most likely in the public mode method's NaN filtering') with the documentation as a supporting premise (item 1, 'contrary to StatUtils.mode documentation and test expectations'), so ENTRY_POINT_BIAS is primary; CONVENTION_PRIOR is present but subordinate and is displaced from the secondary slot by the integration finding, which is what distinguishes this run from run-004. Partly defensible on the same documented-promise grounds as the other facade runs; body is a null check plus delegation (line 822, displayed via grep at call 5).

Both labellers agree on the pair and that the divergence was located at the gold (item 4: 'FastMath.tabulate adds every double value, including NaN, to a Frequency; Frequency.getMode returns keys with the maximum count', four NaNs beating three zeros and twos; tabulate requested at call 8, sed 1120-1165, and re-read line-numbered at call 15 of 19, nl 1132-1145; frozen full_gold_read=true). The rank-1 justification is item 2: 'StatUtils.mode documents that NaN values are ignored, but delegates directly to BlockFieldMatrix.leadingValues' with the inference 'The public API method is the strongest localization target because its contract is violated and it controls delegation.' The explicit because-clause is the documented contract, so CONVENTION_PRIOR is primary; 'public API method' and 'controls delegation' are the entry-point premises, so ENTRY_POINT_BIAS is secondary. The gold is ranked third behind mostFrequent although item 4 indicts only tabulate. Partly defensible: the facade carries the only documented NaN promise on the path and returns NaN on the trigger; its body is a null check plus delegation (lines 818-822 at call 15), so the omitted guard is tabulate's.

Agreement on the pair and on divergence at the gold (item 3: 'FastMath.tabulate adds every Double value to Frequency, including Double.NaN' and 'Counting NaN before mode selection explains why the NaN-heavy sample returns NaN'; the full body including lines 1140-1141 is visible in the safe view at call 9 of 14, its only display, together with FrequencyTest's NaN tests used to demote Frequency). Rank 1 rests on item 1 alone: 'The mode computation counts NaN values, contradicting StatUtils.mode documentation that NaNs are ignored', candidate_methods [StatUtils::mode], references StatUtils.java 808-823. The justification is the documented contract, so CONVENTION_PRIOR is primary and ENTRY_POINT_BIAS secondary (first code read was the entry point at call 4; calls 11-13 returned to StatUtils' test body and the stale java.util.List import, hunting for edit footprints at the entry point). The gold is ranked third behind mostFrequent despite item 3. Partly defensible on the facade's documented NaN promise, violated on the trigger; its body is a one-line delegation.

Both labellers agree ENTRY_POINT_BIAS is primary and that the divergence was not located at the gold; they split on the secondary. Rank 1 rests on item 1: 'The failing test exercises StatUtils.mode and expects NaN inputs to be ignored' with the inference 'The public mode contract is violated specifically for NaN handling', and the other nine entries follow the call chain in top-down order (item 3: 'Methods on this chain are the most likely locations'), mostFrequent above tabulate. The justification is being the test-exercised public method whose expected behaviour fails, and the ordering is by distance from the entry point, so ENTRY_POINT_BIAS is primary; the 'contract' wording gives CONVENTION_PRIOR a presence but not the secondary slot. DISCOVERY_WITHOUT_INSPECTION is not warranted and EVIDENCE_INTEGRATION_FAILURE is: the safe view truncates the outputs, but call 9 requested FastMath 1115-1165 and call 18 requested nl 1130-1148, both ranges enclosing tabulate (1130-1144), and frozen gold_exposed=true / full_gold_read=true confirm display; the agent also ran its own probe (call 11: mode(nanInfested) -> [NaN], mode({NaN,NaN}) -> [NaN]) and displayed Frequency.addValue/incrementValue (calls 13, 18). Its item 2 inference, 'NaN values are being included in the frequency calculation', names the mechanism that only tabulate's loop performs, yet tabulate is listed merely as a hop and ranked third. Partly defensible on the facade's documented NaN promise (javadoc 808-810 and 834-836 displayed at calls 5, 16 and 18); its body is a null check plus delegation.

defensibility_rule_applied: A rank-1 method is 'partly' defensible only when its own documentation states an obligation that the trigger input observably violates, even though its body contains no faulty statement and the omitted logic lives elsewhere; it is 'no' when its only claim is being called by the test, lying on the call path, or being the method that forms the output, while its documentation is silent on the violated property; 'yes' would require the rank-1 body itself to contain the omission. Applied to B4: StatUtils.mode carries the only 'NaN values are ignored' promise on the path (javadoc lines 808 and 834), returns NaN on the trigger, and the pre-variant code kept the isNaN guard inside StatUtils' own private helper (visible in the removed hunk of variant.patch), so a careful engineer could place a pre-delegation filter there, but its body is a null check plus a one-line delegation (both overloads), and the guard the variant dropped is in FastMath.tabulate's loop; hence every facade-rank-1 run (7C06F2/run-004, 7C06F2/run-005, CCA96B/run-001, CCA96B/run-004, CCA96B/run-005) is 'partly', uniformly, regardless of whether the chain located the divergence. MathArrays.mostFrequent (7C06F2/run-003) documents only 'most frequently occurring value(s) ... in ascending order', which [NaN] literally satisfies, and no in-method filter can recover [0, 2] once NaN has out-counted 0 and 2 in the Frequency table, so it is 'no'.
